headline: Schema-driven tools make microbial and synthetic biology metadata machine-actionable
label: Machine Actionable Metadata Infrastructure
summary: Standardized identifiers, explicit schemas and LLM-based annotation now let genomic and experimental metadata be validated, mapped and reused at scale.
synthesis: The dominant thread is machine-actionable metadata: records are structured against explicit schemas or standardized identifiers for validation and reuse. ro-crate-rs provides a Rust library with Python API and CLI for building and validating RO-Crate packages in synthetic biology automation. MIFE and MIFD define minimum metadata models for fermentation experiments and devices, implemented as a Python/LinkML package. Ratatoskr retrieves type strain sequences and metadata from LPSN, BacDive and NCBI, resolving synonym-based cross-database identifiers. orthogene standardizes gene identifiers and infers homologs across hundreds of species. On the annotation side, myLLannotator applies a 3B-parameter LLM for zero-shot labeling of microbial genome metadata, while a separate LLM study re-annotates microbiome sample origins validated on 1,000 curated samples. Classification and plasmid tools (HYMET, MADRe, PlasAnn) sit adjacent to this theme rather than within it. What is new is pairing schema-driven specifications with deployable software.
